summary: I harvested the rendered copy of 13 production pages with a Chrome UA (Playwright innerText, plus curl for the listing page and server HTML for /, the ridge subdivision, Awbrey Butte, and /team/matthew-ryan), traced every bad line to its source file, inventoried the mechanical rules that still shape copy after Matt's 2026-09-07 retirement, read the site-queue accept test and TASTE rubric for any voice criterion, and pulled three competitor/place-owner pages for tone. Saved copy, HTML and scripts are under the scratch dir named above; git status is clean and no MCP tool was used. The site's copy has three sources: 27 hand-authored place JSON files with citations (the best writing on the site, e.g. Tetherow and Awbrey Butte about_prose), route-local constants (about/home), and roughly ten TypeScript sentence generators that template figures across ~3,400 subdivision, 28 neighborhood and city/community pages; plus 20 seeded blog spotlights and three broker bios in Supabase that render only on /team/<slug>. Grok is not used for public place copy. The 'awful voice' is mostly the generators and the source lines: engineer-first traces are auto-cut into the visible source name ('market_metric financing_mix', 'leftover membership', 'Median asking price $1'), instruction copy reads as content ('Hover, tap or tab another cut for its home and dollars.'), self-referential sentences ('You are on the Bend housing market report'), templated headings ('Awbrey Butte questions, answered with the number', four bare 'Bend' H2s), raw MLS abbreviations on /price-drops ('Bend · Oww', 'La Pine · DrrhLp'), and sentences cut at abbreviations ('Camp Abbot, a U.S.'). The one p0 is not voice but shipped data: components/motion/number.tsx AnimatedNumber defaults settleOnMount=false and renders format(0) on the server, so the server HTML of / carries '$0 median list price' and 'houses for sale 0' for every community and city card, and /subdivisions/ridge-at-eagle-crest ships 'The middle asking price of the 0 homes for sale … is $0' beside '88 homes' and '14 homes' for the same phrase; five islands never pass settleOnMount. Nothing in the loop reads text: the site-queue accept test is catalog/tokens/floor/score, the TASTE rubric has no copy row, the evaluator scores screenshots, and the content floor counts words, which rewards more sentences. Surviving mechanical residue is small: the em-dash lock (Matt 2026-09-20, a 22-path allowlist), a banned-word regex in check-market-narrative-integrity, ten dead 'brand-voice:exempt' markers. I also observed intermittent production 502s ('upstream request failed') on 4 of ~22 loads. Proposal: one voice model plus per-class exemplar files that generators must draw from, a separate text-reading evaluator recorded as voiceReview beside tasteReview, decidable gates only for honesty and jargon (settleOnMount, reader-facing source names, publishPlatDisplayName everywhere, no URL paths in prose), and surfacing the copy that already sounds right (bios, VOICE.md homepage lead, about_prose paragraphs).

findings.title: AnimatedNumber ships 0 / $0 figures in server HTML on home, city, neighborhood and subdivision pages
findings.claim: Five client islands render figures through the beUI AnimatedNumber with its default settleOnMount=false, so the server-rendered face is format(0): every homepage community card reads '$0 median list price / 0 homes for sale', every town reads 'houses for sale 0', and every subdivision insight reads 'The middle asking price of the 0 homes for sale in {plat} is $0'. A crawler or answer engine reading raw HTML, and any reader whose motion never settles, gets a fabricated zero.
findings.evidence: home-raw.html `$0…median list price` and `houses for sale 0`; ridge-raw.html 'The middle asking price of the 0 homes for sale in Ridge at Eagle Crest is $0'; components/motion/number.tsx lines 14-27 and useState(settleOnMount ? value : 0); grep: 13 usages, 5 with settleOnMount; scroll-test.mjs still shows 9 zero cards after scrolling (crawler-renderer behavior UNVERIFIED).
findings.why_it_matters: §0 forbids a wrong number in front of a human or a crawler; the primitive's own comment says so. It also makes the voice absurd ('$0 median list price') on the highest-traffic page and on 3,427 subdivision pages, and the homepage is the page an AI engine quotes first.
findings.proposed_fix: Flip the default in components/motion/number.tsx to settleOnMount=true (animate only on later value changes), or forbid direct AnimatedNumber imports outside components/motion and route everything through V3Number. Add a gate: any `<AnimatedNumber` in app/ or components/ (outside components/motion) without settleOnMount fails. Verify with Search Console URL Inspection rendered HTML on / and one /subdivisions/* page.

findings.title: Visible source names are auto-cut from engineer-first traces ('market_metric financing_mix', 'leftover membership', 'Median asking price $1')
findings.claim: V3SourceLine derives the visible 'Source' name by cutting the trace at the first comma or stop, and most traces open with a table, column or internal layer name, so visitors read database identifiers as the source of a figure; one cut lands inside a thousands-formatted price and prints 'Median asking price $1'.
findings.evidence: awbrey-raw.html v3-source__name values 'Median asking price $1' and 'market_metric financing_mix'; listing-raw.html v3-source__name 'leftover membership'; lib/listing/publish-listing-pill-read.ts:84 'Market Truth (market_metric, detached): …'; listing RSC source 'public.market_metric · stat_id=pct_with_price_cut …'; components/site/v3/V3SourceLine.tsx:112-124; lib/place/publish-place-affordability.ts:121,144. lib/site/place-answers.ts:170-186 already moved its machine handle to data-source-key for this exact tell.
findings.why_it_matters: TASTE.md bans 'raw slugs, internal labels, methodology jargon' in anything a visitor reads, and VOICE.md says specific beats generic in a person's words. A reader cannot check 'leftover membership'; an answer engine may quote it. '$1' is a false number.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `name` a required, reader-facing prop on V3SourceLine (e.g. 'Bend detached closed sales, last 12 months') and move the machine handle to data-source-key like place-answers does; fix the comma in publish-place-affordability.ts:121; add a decidable gate that the rendered v3-source__name may not match /(public\.|market_metric|_mv\b|stat_id=|leftover|[a-z]+_[a-z]+)/ or end in a truncated currency.

findings.title: Raw MLS subdivision abbreviations leak on /price-drops and the Atlas pulse
findings.claim: Price-drop rows print the MLS SubdivisionName through displaySubdivision (a sentinel filter), not publishPlatDisplayName, so visitors read 'Oww', 'DrrhLp', 'Mob Pk', 'Trac', 'Inn Of The 7th'; the About atlas pulse prints 'PrineVille - Second'. The founding case of ci:publish-place-names was this exact defect on another route.
findings.evidence: price-drops.txt lines 129-147; about.txt line 286; app/price-drops/_v3/drops-field-items.ts:66; lib/slug.ts:34-41; scripts/check-publish-place-names.mjs header ('More areas printed Oww / DrrhTrs').
findings.why_it_matters: It is the most visible jargon on a page built to be shared weekly, it names places no buyer recognizes, and the gate that exists for it does not cover the route.
findings.proposed_fix: Route every visitor-facing subdivision label (price drops, atlas pulse, listing cards, similar-homes lines) through publishPlatDisplayName (withhold abbreviations) and extend ci:publish-place-names to pin those call sites.

findings.title: Nothing in the loop reads the text: no voice criterion in the accept test, the TASTE rubric or the evaluator
findings.claim: The site-queue accept test is catalog/tokens/content-floor/score; the TASTE rubric has no copy row; the frozen evaluator scores screenshots; the content floor counts words. Copy therefore drifts toward templated headings and instruction sentences that a screenshot cannot flag, and adding sentences is rewarded.
findings.evidence: .claude/skills/site-queue/SKILL.md lines 55-80; design_system/public/TASTE.md rubric table; taste-evaluator.v1-2026-09-12.md (shotsHash, only 'raw slugs' tell touches copy); repeated production phrases: '{place} questions, answered with the number' on 3 grains, 'how we calculate this' 14x on /cities/bend, four bare 'Bend' H2s, 'Hover, tap or tab another cut…', 'You are on the Bend housing market report…'.
findings.why_it_matters: Matt's complaint is the voice, and the only feedback loop the builders optimize against cannot see it. VOICE.md retired mechanical rules, which leaves human-quality judgment as the mechanism, and no human or model is assigned to read the words.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a separate text-reading evaluator per page class (innerText, chrome stripped), scored on: sounds like a person who knows Central Oregon, jargon/identifiers, repetition (same phrase >2x per page), self-reference, fragments, fake precision; record it as voiceReview beside tasteReview in parity.json with builder ≠ evaluator and the same rise discipline; drop the word count from the content floor as a quality proxy. Matt reads one page per class per round.

findings.evidence: app/page.tsx:186 ('Written valuation in 24 hours'); app/about/_v3/about-constants.ts:107; sell.txt lines 197-200 and 237.
findings.why_it_matters: They are promises a licensed broker is held to, and one missed 24-hour valuation makes the FAQ schema false.
findings.proposed_fix: Matt confirms each as a standing commitment (then it ships as 'we send…' with the commitment named in the plan) or it is softened to the condition ('the day after photos come back').

findings.title: firstSentence cuts blurbs at abbreviations ('Camp Abbot, a U.S.', 'off O.B.')
findings.claim: The homepage community cards and trail overviews take the first sentence of authored prose with a regex that stops at any period, so a sentence containing 'U.S.' or 'O.B.' ships truncated.
findings.evidence: home.txt line 370; cities-bend.txt line 2560; lib/site/place-recreation.ts:37-43; app/_v3/home-featured-communities.ts:113-130 (imports firstSentence from app/cities/_v3/cities-index-constants).
findings.why_it_matters: A cut sentence on the homepage reads as broken to a person and as low quality to an engine.
findings.proposed_fix: Author a one-line `blurb` field in the 27 place JSON files and trail registry (no splitting), or make the splitter abbreviation-aware and require the result to end in a full stop after a lowercase word.

findings.title: Heading hygiene the naked-verb gate cannot see (bare place-name H2s, fragments, all-caps, middle dots)
findings.claim: Headings on the harvested pages include four bare 'Bend' H2s and three 'Awbrey Butte' H2s, 'Single-family in Bend' as an H1, 'HOMES FOR SALE' and 'RIDGE AT EAGLE CREST RIGHT NOW' all-caps H2s, 'About Ryan Realty · Bend' and 'The brokers' as H1s, 'The window', 'Reach list', 'Where to next', 'Run the number both ways', and '{place} questions, answered with the number' on three grains; the closed 10-word naked-verb list catches none of these.
findings.evidence: H1/H2 arrays in cities-bend.txt, cities-bend-awbrey-butte.txt, cities-bend-types-single-family.txt, subdivisions-ridge-at-eagle-crest.txt, about.txt, team.txt; scripts/check-naked-verb-headings.mjs lines 34-37.
findings.why_it_matters: Headings are what search snippets and answer engines lift; VOICE.md's retired line 'headings say something specific' is still the right bar and nothing enforces or reviews it.
findings.proposed_fix: Per-class heading exemplars in the exemplar files (VOICE-4) plus a decidable check that an H2 is not identical to the page's place name and not all-caps; rename the three templated section headings to the question they answer.

findings.title: Mechanical residue after the 2026-09-07 retirement: dead exempt markers, a banned-word regex, an allowlisted em-dash gate
findings.claim: Ten '// brand-voice:exempt' markers remain for a deleted gate; check-market-narrative-integrity keeps BANNED_WORDS/BANNED_PUNCT (contradicting 'no word lists', though scoped to one file); the em-dash lock (Matt 2026-09-20, which post-dates and overrides VOICE.md on this point) scans a 22-path allowlist while generator directories outside it hold 58 U+2014 literals (mostly §0 traces; visible leakage was 2 em dashes across 13 pages).
findings.evidence: grep counts (10 exempt markers; 58 em-dash hits in lib/site, lib/place, app/subdivisions, app/communities, app/listing, components/site/v3); scripts/check-market-narrative-integrity.mjs:79-80; scripts/check-no-public-em-dash.mjs:28-52; per-page em-dash counts sell 1, ridge 1.
findings.why_it_matters: Contradictory residue is what makes an agent unsure which rule binds; the em-dash gate's coverage gap means the lock is a list, not a rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the exempt markers; keep part A (numbers trace) of the narrative gate and drop parts B's word list; make the em-dash gate walk all public string literals under app/ (non-admin), components/site, lib/site, lib/place, lib/listing with the same AST visitor it already has.

findings.title: Seeded blog spotlights (20 posts) with stock heroes and portal-guide phrasing surface as 'area guide' rows on community pages
findings.claim: Community pages pull reading rows from blog_posts seeded by scripts/blog-content/community-spotlights.ts; the Tetherow post is titled 'Tetherow Where Resort Living Meets Real Estate', its excerpt promises 'what that actually means for your wallet and lifestyle', and its hero is an Unsplash stock photo, so the brand's best-sourced place page ends on a generic guide.
findings.evidence: communities-tetherow.txt lines 497-498; scripts/blog-content/community-spotlights.ts:580-595 (title, excerpt, hero_image_url images.unsplash.com); 20 `title:` entries in the file.
findings.why_it_matters: These posts carry the brand into search results for '{community} guide' queries and they read like every other portal's guide; the stock hero contradicts the locked hero-photo rule in CLAUDE.md §3.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-edit the 20 seeds against VOICE.md (specific, first person plural, no 'here is what it means for your wallet'), replace hero_image_url with the community's own photo from the asset library, and re-seed.

findings.title: Intermittent HTTP 502 'upstream request failed' from production during the harvest
findings.claim: Four of roughly twenty-two production loads in forty minutes returned a 502 body 'upstream request failed' (first load of /subdivisions/ridge-at-eagle-crest, two of three homepage loads in scroll-test.mjs) and /about logged a 502 resource; a crawler hitting that response indexes nothing.
findings.evidence: harvest-index.json (status 502, innerText 'upstream request failed'); scroll-test.mjs output for two contexts; about.txt CONSOLE_ERRORS. Cause UNVERIFIED: all requests traverse the sandbox proxy; the body text is an origin-style error, not a proxy page. Outside this reader's area; recorded for the seo-technical reader.
findings.why_it_matters: A 502 to Googlebot or an AI crawler directly suppresses visibility and is the first thing to rule out when rankings slip.
findings.proposed_fix: The seo-technical/infra lane checks Vercel function errors and timeouts for the place and home routes over the last 7 days and correlates with Search Console crawl stats; if the origin is throwing, add the route to the degraded-ISR path so a cached page serves instead of a 502.
